name: Motion & animation
blurb: UI and web motion that feels right: easing, timing, GSAP, scroll, React, Reanimated, Lottie, Three.js and Manim.
searches: CSS scroll-driven animations view transitions browser support update
agent skill UI animation easing Claude

tests.prompt: Our dropdown menu opens with `transition: all 400ms ease-in` from `transform: scale(0)`. Review it and give me the fixed CSS, including reduced motion.
tests.good: Flags all three problems (animating `all`, ease-in on an entrance, scale from 0). Uses a strong ease-out such as cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) at 150–250 ms, starts from scale about 0.95 plus opacity, sets transform-origin at the trigger, and adds a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that keeps an opacity or instant change.

tests.prompt: Build a pinned product section in Next.js: while the user scrolls 3 screens, three feature cards slide in one after another and a phone mockup rotates slightly. Use GSAP.
tests.good: Uses useGSAP with a scope ref and 'use client', one timeline with ScrollTrigger pin and scrub, ease none on scrubbed tweens, and transforms only. Wraps everything in gsap.matchMedia with a reduced-motion branch, gives the end in scroll distance (e.g. +=300%), and cleans up automatically.

tests.prompt: Make a 1.5-second SVG logo reveal for our splash screen: the mark draws on, then the wordmark letters cascade in. Give me the HTML and tell me how to check the final frame matches the logo exactly.
tests.good: One element per semantic part with ids, pathLength=1 draw-on, letters staggered with overlap, a timing split of about 20/50/30, and literal easing inside @keyframes with fill-mode both. Adds a reduced-motion final state and a ?t= seek hook, and checks frames (including the last) against the static logo.

tests.prompt: Our landing page needs a pinned scroll section where our smart kettle turns 180 degrees as the user scrolls, with three feature captions fading in. We have no product frames yet, so generate them, and keep the page fast on phones.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the frames through image-creation (editing-references-consistency.md: one product reference, fixed lighting and lens, even angle steps, no drift between frames), the scene here (motion-principles.md, scroll-animation.md, gsap.md: ScrollTrigger pin with scrub, canvas frame sequence, ease none on scrubbed tweens, end set as scroll distance), and page speed through website-building (performance-cwv.md: first frame as the poster, the rest loaded lazily, LCP and CLS checked on mobile). Transforms and opacity only; reduced motion shows one still with the captions; first, middle and last frames checked; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our designer sent onboarding-hero.aep from After Effects: a 4-second illustration with shape layers, a Trim Paths draw-on, a wiggle() expression on floating dots, a precomp under an alpha track matte, a Gaussian Blur glow and a live text layer in our brand font. We need it in our React Native app and on the web as a small Lottie that looks the same everywhere. Tell me exactly how to export it, what will break, and how you'll check it before we ship.
tests.good: Exports with Bodymovin or the LottieFiles for After Effects plugin (JSON or .lottie/dotLottie), with text either converted to shapes or exported as glyphs, hidden layers skipped and images not embedded unless needed. Flags each risky feature against the official Lottie supported-features table, whose columns are Android, iOS (Core Animation and Main Thread), Windows and Web (SVG, Canvas, HTML); dotLottie players are not in that table and need their own test: the wiggle() expression must be baked to keyframes (Convert Expression to Keyframes) because the native players don't run expressions, the Gaussian Blur glow is replaced by a shape or opacity trick, and the track matte, merge paths and live font are tested on each platform. Keeps the file small (fewer shape groups and keyframes, sensible frame rate, a size budget stated and measured) and plays it with lottie-react-native or the dotLottie player with explicit autoplay and loop, showing a static final frame under reduced motion. Checks first, middle and last frames in a local player (such as Skottie or the LottieFiles preview) and on a real iOS and Android device against an After Effects render of the same frames. Does not claim to open or edit the .aep without After Effects (or a local AE MCP bridge the user has installed), says what it could not verify, and asks before uploading the file to any third-party site.

tools.name: GSAP
tools.why: Industry-standard timeline/scroll animation library, about 2.2% of all websites and 2.15M weekly npm downloads (annnimate State of Web Animation 2026); Webflow made the whole ecosystem including plugins free in 2025.

tools.name: Motion (Framer Motion)
tools.why: Most downloaded animation library, roughly 33 to 37M weekly npm downloads and 16M+ monthly (npm trends, annnimate, Motion docs), though some counts are transitive via UI kits.

tools.name: Lottie / dotLottie (LottieFiles)
tools.why: Default vector animation interchange format for web and mobile; recommended in every 2026 round-up (Timace, xcodx, annnimate); dotlottie-web has 892 stars with a Rust/ThorVG runtime, and LottieFiles ships an official Lottie Creator MCP.

tools.name: Rive
tools.why: Standard tool for interactive state-machine vector animation across web, React, React Native, Flutter, Apple, Android and Unity; named alongside Lottie in every 2026 round-up, and Rive shipped an official editor MCP.

tools.name: React Native Reanimated
tools.why: The default animation engine for React Native and Expo; Reanimated 4 is the current stable release (Software Mansion docs) and Software Mansion publishes official agent skills for it.

tools.name: CSS animations, WAAPI and View Transitions
tools.why: 91.7% of mobile pages use a CSS transition versus 18.4% that load any JS animation library (annnimate State of Web Animation 2026); it is the cheapest-tool-first default.

tools.name: Three.js
tools.why: Dominant WebGL/WebGPU 3D library; its animation system (mixer, clips, morph targets) is the standard route for 3D motion on the web (three.js docs, 2026 round-ups).

tools.name: After Effects (with Bodymovin / LottieFiles plugin)
tools.why: The standard motion-design app: in School of Motion's 2019 survey of 1,000+ motion designers nearly 8 in 10 worked primarily in After Effects, and 2026 round-ups (LottieFiles 'Best motion design tools ranked by use case', Guideflow, MotionMedia) still call it the default production tool. It is also the main Lottie authoring source via Bodymovin / LottieFiles for AE. No official Adobe MCP for AE; community MCP bridges exist (Dakkshin/after-effects-mcp, 703 stars, MIT; kumoproductions/mcp-aftereffects). The guides only mention it as the Lottie export source.

tools.name: Remotion
tools.why: Leading React-based programmatic video framework; its official agent-skills repo has 4.8k stars (GitHub), and the guides already treat it as the comparison point for frame-pure rendering.

tools.name: Anime.js
tools.why: Lightweight multi-target animation engine, now at v4.0 per its docs; named in 2026 round-ups of free JS animation libraries (SmashingApps, Timace).

tools.name: Manim (Community Edition)
tools.why: Standard Python library for programmatic maths and algorithm explainer animation (3Blue1Brown lineage); a 1.1k-star MIT skill exists for it.

tools.name: Spline
tools.why: Browser-based design tool for interactive 3D scenes with embeddable runtime; Spline's docs list a Spline MCP server and an in-editor AI agent.

tools.name: Cinema 4D (Maxon)
tools.why: The standard 3D app for motion designers: Maxon calls its MoGraph toolset 'the industry standard for procedural motion design', 2026 round-ups (Guideflow, MotionMedia, Fox Render Farm) name it the favourite for 3D motion graphics, and School of Motion's 2025 review lists AE and Cinema 4D as the foundational motion tools. Pairs with After Effects through Cineware. Modelling itself belongs to 3d-modeling; MoGraph animation and the AE hand-off belong here. No official MCP or agent skill found (gh search: only a 1-star script repo).

tools.name: Figma Motion
tools.why: Figma's native timeline animation tool, launched at Config 2026 (24 June) and in open beta on all plans: keyframes, presets, easing and timing variables, animated components; Dev Mode shows a read-only timeline and copies code as CSS, JSON or motion.dev, and Figma says animated frames pass to coding agents through the Figma MCP server. Too new to call major, but Figma's reach makes it the likely designer-to-code motion source. Smart Animate prototype settings stay with figma-design; turning either into code is this craft's job.

tools.name: Jitter
tools.why: Browser-based collaborative motion tool for UI micro-interactions, product and social animations from Figma designs; about 1.3M monthly visitors (Capterra/Tracxn profiles) and ranked in LottieFiles' and ProductHub's 2026 tool round-ups as the fastest path from a static design to a moving asset. Small seed company, so minor. No API, MCP or agent skill found.

tools.name: Cavalry
tools.why: Procedural 2D animation app for macOS and Windows (v2.8 per its docs), used for data-driven motion and generating many variations; LottieFiles' 2026 ranking lists it as 'the procedural powerhouse' beside After Effects. Niche next to AE, so minor. No MCP or agent skill found.
